--- PART 3/6 ---

STRATEGY: Parent defects at n>95 when the last two opponent moves are C, giving an endgame payoff of 15 against slot3 but only 8 against TFT. The trace simulates alternative endgame defection start points (n=96, n=97, n=98) against all 12 opponents, computing payoffs and comparing totals. It considers changing the parent's endgame start to n=97 (defect at rounds 98–100) as a compromise, finding it slightly better on average against the pool (+0.2 vs the n=98 start) but worse against TFT.

STRATEGY: Parent (slot10) uses complex non-endgame logic with endgame defection at n>95 (rounds 97-100). The trace manually simulates S (defect at n>=97) and U (defect at n>=96) against 12 opponents, then compares Parent vs S, finding S better by 6.4 points. It proposes adopting slot3's Tit-for-two-tats logic with endgame changed from remaining<=2 (n>=98) to remaining<=3 (n>=97), and considers an adaptive probe to distinguish TFT-like from forgiving opponents.

ORIGIN: NONE

STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT-like strategy that retaliates immediately to a single defection. The trace simulates an adaptive revision that cooperates for five rounds, defects once as a probe, then classifies the opponent as retaliatory or forgiving based on their response. It changes the endgame timing and mid-game exploitation: cautious mode cooperates until n>=99 then defects, while exploit mode defects more often and starts endgame earlier (n>=96).
